scope: Read-only independent preliminary review of T2 R1 stopped bytes. No source, test, Git, external, Vault, or network mutation. One bounded public-API reproduction used a disposable /private/tmp fixture with a copied/rehashed plan artifact only.

findings.title: Rehashed full plan can omit live chunks and still finalize as complete
findings.observation: A disposable workspace with 50 live chunks and a normal two-batch full plan was copied into a new job whose inventory/partition contained one chunk. Recomputed plan_id and plan_sha256 were valid. Public export_knowledge_batch, import_knowledge_batch, export_knowledge_merge_context, import_knowledge_merge, and finalize_knowledge_batches all returned OK; finalize advanced_head=true and reported planned_chunks=processed_chunks=1, batch_count=1, gap_chunk_ids=[], while the live source contained 50 chunks.
findings.expected: A plan must be bound to the exact current derived-chunk inventory and complete partition before export/import/finalize; caller-controlled rehashing is not source authority.

findings.title: Zero-batch refresh trusts a caller-rehashed seed document
findings.observation: For a refresh plan with an empty partition, seed_document is checked only as a dict with matching paper_id/schema. Finalization returns it directly and does not run _validate_document against live evidence before rendering/publishing. A rehashed seed can cite one retained live chunk and omit sections/chunks while producing a structurally valid record.
findings.expected: Validate the seed document against the current live evidence and exact complete inventory even when batch_count is zero; retain only safely remapped base content.

findings.title: Accepted batch persistence is not bound to its own partition citations
findings.observation: _valid_accepted_batch checks only shape, plan/source identity, document self-hash, and context hash format. It does not validate the document or require cited IDs to belong to plan.partition[batch_index]. Later merge evidence is a union over all accepted batch partition IDs, so a persisted accepted JSON whose document was rewritten and rehashed can cite another accepted batch’s chunk and pass merge citation checks.
findings.expected: Revalidate each persisted accepted document against its exact batch partition and live chunk identities before it can be used by merge/finalize/classification.

findings.title: Processing-complete provenance accepts pending or non-final merge steps
findings.observation: validate_job_provenance permits both completed and pending jobs. With a merge hash it returns true for any accepted merge step, not specifically the final contiguous step; with merge_sha256=None it returns true for any pending plan. Extended coverage still declares processing_complete=true, so a self-consistent record can claim complete full/refresh coverage while its job is incomplete or its provenance points to an earlier step.
findings.expected: Require completed classification, exact accepted batch/merge sets, and the final merge hash/document binding for processing_complete records; zero-batch is the only null-merge exception.

findings.title: Record ancestry validates existence/cycles but not same-paper edge semantics
findings.observation: On the stopped Builder-modified bytes, the recursion checks active-stack cycles before the validated set, so a valid shared-base selection DAG is accepted; the earlier suspected global-seen false-cycle observation is excluded. The remaining gap is semantic: referenced base/candidate IDs are only required to be valid bundles and acyclic. Their paper_id and mode-specific relationship are not checked, so a rehashed refresh/selection record for paper A can reference valid records for paper B or an unrelated branch.
findings.expected: For each ancestry edge, require the referenced record to have the child paper_id and the wrapper/schema relation required by refresh versus selection.
